common_name: Wuzi Chinese Bayberry (Female Tissue-Cultured Yangmei Clone)

planting.note: Set out a tissue-cultured female clone in spring on a sharply drained, acidic site, and plan ahead for a male yangmei within pollinator range since this named selection will not set fruit alone. A raised bed or berm helps on the heavier clay soils common along the Gulf Coast.

directions: Wuzi is a named female clone of yangmei propagated by tissue culture rather than grown from seed, giving more predictable fruiting age and fruit quality than unselected seedling bayberry trees. It needs strongly acidic, fast-draining soil and resents both soggy low spots and heavy feeding, so go easy on fertilizer and keep it off poorly drained clay. Young trees are tender to hard freezes and benefit from winter protection for their first several years, after which the tree becomes moderately drought tolerant and handles brief cold dips typical of zone 8-9 winters. Site a compatible male bayberry nearby, since female clones like Wuzi depend on outside pollen to produce the bumpy, sweet-tart berries each early summer.
sources: Woodlanders Nursery — Myrica rubra Yangmei cultivation notes
